questions.q: 3,3-Dimethylbut-1-ene is treated with (i) Hg(OAc)₂, H₂O/THF and (ii) NaBH₄, OH⁻. The product is:
questions.explain: Water adds Markovnikov and no carbocation forms, so the skeleton stays intact. 2,3-Dimethylbutan-2-ol is the rearranged product of dilute-acid hydration, and the 1-ol would be the hydroboration product.

questions.q: Why does oxymercuration–demercuration give no rearranged products?
options: The intermediate is a bridged mercurinium ion, not a free carbocation
Water adds before the electrophile does
The reaction is a concerted syn addition with no intermediate
questions.explain: Mercury bridges both carbons, so there is no open carbocation to undergo hydride or alkyl shifts. A concerted syn addition with no intermediate describes hydroboration, not oxymercuration.

questions.q: Propene is treated with Hg(OAc)₂ in methanol, and the product is reduced with NaBH₄. The final product is:
questions.explain: In alkoxymercuration the alcohol solvent opens the mercurinium ion at the more substituted carbon, so after reduction the OCH₃ is on C-2. Propan-2-ol would form only if water were the nucleophile.

questions.q: Which statement about the stereochemistry of oxymercuration–demercuration of a simple alkene is correct?
options: Water adds anti in step (i), but the radical demercuration step scrambles the overall H/OH relationship
The overall addition of H and OH is always syn
The overall addition of H and OH is always anti
Both steps are stereospecific, giving a single stereoisomer
questions.explain: Water attacks the mercurinium ion from the face opposite to mercury, but NaBH₄ replaces Hg through radicals, so the final H and OH may be cis or trans. A fixed relationship is seen only in rigid substrates such as norbornene.
